answer: Bond each identity and audit a random island of voters every round. A fake found there is slashed along with the guarantor who staked for it, so casting n Sybil votes means locking n separate bonds and still absorbing the audit loss: the attacker's cost rises linearly while each extra vote is worth the same. The ridge in the voucher graph matters too, because each new fake needs a distinct sponsor with real stake at risk. Even minting saffron tokens to buy those sponsors requires the same collateral, so a large attack always costs more than the votes it buys.
